newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sterling may have peaked against US$ - The Times.
newsitem.headline: Sterling may have peaked against US$ - The Times.

text.p: Sterling's recent rise against the U.S. dollar may have run out of steam after it hit the US$1.70 level, The Times of London's Anatole Kaletsky said in the newspaper's Internet edition.
Sterling rose sharply in Asia during morning trading on rumours that Kaletsky had forecast sterling would rise to three marks. The article did not mention three marks as a target.

Saying the mark was set to become the world's weakest major currency, he added that, "If the dollar rises eventually to at least 1.70 marks, sterling will have to fall quite sharply against the greenback to avoid moving back to the old ERM zone above 2.80 marks."

Kaletsky said the futures market was forecasting a rise in three-month interest rates from 6.5 percent today to 7.4 percent in December. He said a modest fiscal tightening would be enough to keep base rates at seven percent or below.
"This would take much of the pressure off the pound," he added.
At 0335 GMT, sterling was quoted at 2.6787/97 marks compared with late European quotes on Thursday of 2.6647/57 and at US$1.6979/89 against late European quotes of 1.6915/22.
